newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian brewery Karlovacka climbs to record high.
newsitem.headline: Croatian brewery Karlovacka climbs to record high.

text.p: Croatian brewery Karlovacka Pivovara hit a new high of 610 kuna in Thursday morning trade, dealers said.
"Karlovacka is still in the spotlight, although the overall intensity of trading has weakened," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.
He said some 900 shares had been traded by noon in a dormant market that slowed down ahead of summer holidays.
Most of the shares were sold for around 600 kuna, after one deal was struck at the record 610 kuna, 20 kuna up on Wednesday's close, Zelimorski said.
He said latest bid was at 605 kuna with an asking price of 615.
Some traders said earlier they expected the share to hit resistance at 600 kuna, after rising steadily from 360 kuna two weeks ago on strong 1996 results.
On June 4, daily newspaper Vecernji List reported the brewer made net profits of 41.2 million kuna after 23.1 million in 1995 and that it hopes for a net profit of 48 million kuna in 1997.
Compania Cervecarias Unidas, based in Chile, has a 66.99 percent stake in Karlovacka Pivovara.
